I · Persistence & resumption ○○ 2026-08-16
Five of the session header’s nine fields describe where the session came from rather than what is in it. What must be saved is everything a scope chain would otherwise ask for at runtime, because at resume time there is no parent to ask. Appending is synchronous and validating — a bad event fails at the call site — while durability is write-behind, and a failed background write is reported without rejecting the producer.
notes/I-persistence-and-resumption.md
I · Persistence & resumption ○○ 2026-08-16
Balance was never about tidiness. repair.ts manufactures the missing tool, step and turn boundaries on reload because they are “needed to resume with a provider-valid transcript” — a tool call with no matching result is invalid on the wire. The property is enforced three times by parties that do not trust each other: the loop’s finally blocks produce it, the token meter throws when it is violated, and repair reconstructs it after a crash.

K · The host boundary ○○ 2026-08-16
The approval seam takes an answerer, not a human — so an ACP client can hold the permission channel. It fails closed at every level, grants are one-shot with no allow-always outcome, and a decision that cannot be logged is not returned: the audit append and the decision commit together, so no granted permission can exist unwritten. The web UI does nothing structural headless cannot; it composes an answerer.
notes/K-the-host-boundary.md
K · The host boundary ○○ 2026-08-16
Neither app is the harness. apps/cli is six files importing only cordis and four boot helpers — it resolves a profile and starts a plugin graph — while the real boundary is a 4,565-line RPC surface every UI is a client of. ACP exposes the same core to programs, carrying prompt text, assistant text, cancellation and one-shot permission decisions.

F · Delegation & sub-agents ○○ 2026-08-16
dsh spawns the real Claude Code Agent SDK and codex app-server as sub-agents. The inheritance guarantees stop at the process boundary — the foreign drivers seed no delegated policy — and the config surface says so: maxDepth accepts provider-managed, and a numeric cap against a provider without a depthLimit capability fails at mount rather than silently.
notes/F-delegation-and-subagents.md
F · Delegation & sub-agents ○○ 2026-08-16
Delegation is the one recursion budget in a harness with no step cap: maxDepth defaults to 3, 0 forbids it, and depth is monotone because a resumed child counting from zero could delegate as if top-level. A delegated child’s approval policy is pinned to never, so a sub-agent can never ask a human — you cannot widen permissions by delegating.
notes/F-delegation-and-subagents.md
F · Delegation & sub-agents ○○ 2026-08-16
A child joins its parent’s composition by scope-chain link rather than copy, so it inherits tools, prompt sections and plugins live; per-child restriction intersects on top and can only narrow. Policy is the opposite — captured synchronously before the child’s first await, so a parent that loosens its sandbox afterwards does not loosen the child.

D · Tools & permission ○○ 2026-08-16
A tool never produces model-facing text. execute() returns a canonical JSON value validated against output.schema, and a pure render() projects it into content blocks — which is why results replay, why Code Mode can hand a program the value, and why note 02 saw a structured wrapper where the toy returned a sentence.
notes/D-tools-and-permission.md
D · Tools & permission ○○ 2026-08-16
The permission boundary is three stages, not one: restrict removes a tool from view entirely, the tools/pre-execute waterfall is negotiable and defaults to allow, and guards are deny-only so listener order cannot turn a denial back into permission. dsh did not decline to ask on our headless run — nothing was installed that wanted to be asked.

J · Observability & cost ○○ 2026-08-16
dsh runs unmodified Claude Code and Codex hook configs on its own seams — and a Stop hook that denies forces the turn to continue, unbounded. Both bridges carry TODO(stop-loop-guard) and defer the fix to hook authors, while hardcoding stop_hook_active to false, which is the signal a hook would self-limit with.
notes/J-observability-and-cost.md
J · Observability & cost ○○ 2026-08-16
Nothing inside dsh can stop a run. token-meter takes no settings at all — observation is total and deliberately powerless — and cancel() has four causes of which only user, parent and disposed are ever produced; hook is reserved and has no producer anywhere.

B · The agent loop ○○ 2026-08-16
A turn does not end when the model stops calling tools: the step reason and an empty next-step inbox are both required, so a tool result can extend a turn the model considered over, or end one it wanted to continue.
notes/B-agent-loop.md
B · The agent loop ○○ 2026-08-16
dsh has no step cap anywhere in the repo. The agent loop is three nested loops, its entire config is one concurrency integer, and termination is a closed set of six recorded reasons — one of which only a crash recovery ever writes.
